properties.content:

Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland

Comments: On 4/14/2026, the Department conducted a routine complete inspection of well 4U at the Athena well pad in Washington Township, Westmoreland County. The Erosion and Sedimentation Control General Permit (ESCGP-3) for this well site was issued on 1/10/2022 and expires on 1/09/2027.The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign is installed at the entrance of the access road and is not obscured from view by vegetation, in accordance with 78a.55 (photo 1). The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), Preparedness Prevention and Contingency (PPC) plan, Erosion and Sediment (E and S) inspection log, Safety Data Sheets (SDS), and ESCGP approval letter are onsite (photos 2-5). The ERP and PPC plan appear to contain the sections required by 78a.55. Eight gas wells are onsite that appear to be in production (photo 11). No evidence of a spill, such as staining, was observed on the ground around the gas wells. Well 4U lacks a permanently affixed well tag at the time of inspection (photo 14). The production tanks and the surrounding secondary containment appear to be sound at the time of inspection. The GPU units are placed on raised secondary containment skids, with no fluid leaks observed (photos 12 and 13).The access road and well pad appear to be stable at the time of inspection with no observed concerns relating to accelerated erosion or sedimentation (photos 7, 8, and 10). Some minor sparsely vegetated ares were observed on site during this inspection, such as the location shown in Photo 9. The Department recommends that the operator assess the site for additional sparsely vegetated area areas and conduct mulching and seeding to ensure continued to vegetative growth on site.Based on observations from this inspection, a violation shall be issued for failure to install the API number to well 4U in a permanent manner.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/11/2024 to DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC in Fallowfield Township, Washington county. 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: DIVERSIFIED PROD LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/11/2024
Violation Code: 102.22(a) - SITE STABILIZATION – PERMANENT STABILIZATION – Permitee failed to have site permanently stabilized and protected from accelerated erosion and sedimentation upon final completion of earth disturbance activity.
Violation ID: 8179680
Permit API: 125-22817
Unconventional: No
County: Washington
Municipality: Fallowfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/11/2024
Comments: On 03/11/2024, a follow up inspection was conducted at the Molek F19 well site following violations issued on 12/08/2023 (IR 3657799, Enforcement 419234). I was accompanied by Environmental Trainees Olivia Holley, Madison Raviart, and Christina Mauri (PA DEP).On 12/08/2023, violations of 102.11(a), 102.22(a)2ii, and 78.53 were issued as outstanding for the access road. Inspection from 12/28/2023 noted that the violations were still open, however the operator was in compliance with schedule. On 01/24/2024, the violations were outstanding (IR 3701625). The following was observed:Some stabilization was used along the upper portion of the access road. Several areas throughout the entire access road did not have stabilization on the open soils. I recommend that stabilization is applied (Photos 1-4). Some areas had vegetation establishing (Photos 2, 4, 5).The channel that runs along the access road did not have rip rap or stabilization. Accelerated erosion and sediment accumulation were noted within this channel, which leads to several culverts along the road (Photo 6).The upper culvert, located at 40.113707 -79.966213, had sediment accumulation within the collection point. I recommend that this is addressed (Photo 7). The culvert located at 40.11300, -79.96751 had large amounts of sediment accumulated within the collection point. The culvert was not able to be seen due to the large amount of sediment within this area (Photos 8, 9). Accelerated erosion was noted within the accumulated sediment (Photo 9). The outlet point of this culvert was covered by the roads gravel/dirt, which was causing accelerated erosion and sediment transport towards the vegetation (Photos 10-12). I recommend that this is addressed. The culvert leading to the collection box was not functioning. Sediment was accumulated and an entry point into the pipe was approximately 99% covered. Accelerated erosion and sedimentation throughout the area and vegetation were noted leading from the channel towards the collection box. There was some sediment laden water within this box. This outlets into the vegetation, where sediment accumulation was noted. The vegetation was accumulating water, which leads towards the stream within the wood line (Photos 13-19). The lower culvert outlets into a channel. Sediment accumulation was noted within the channel. I recommend that rip rap is used within this channel, as this leads directly to the stream (Photos 20, 21).The culverts along the first portion of the access road, near the site gate, were not cleaned out. Potholes along the road were not addressed. Channelization was noted leading from the potholes off of the road. The beginning of the access road, where it meets the township road, was not addressed. This area was previously displaying high levels of flow, leading onto the township road, and depositing sediment. This was noted within IR 3701625, photos 24 and 15 (Photos 22-25). The violations issued on 01/24/2024, IR 3701625, remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 4/10/2023 to BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC in Springfield Twp, Bradford county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BLACKHILL ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 4/10/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 991391
Permit API: 015-23733
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Springfield Twp
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 4/10/2023
Comments: The Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a follow-up inspection of Blackhill Energy's (Blackhill) Jackson A well site located in Springfield Township, Bradford County on 4/10/2023 at 1525 hours. The weather was 67 degrees with clear skies. The inspection was conducted to evaluate remedial activities that were conducted after a release that occurred on 4/6/2023.Moody and Associates Inc. (Moody's)(Environmental consultant) was onsite during my inspection and have been conducting field screenings for Blackhill. Since the release that occurred on 4/6/2023, Blackhill has had the entire southern stormwater conveyance channel excavated (photos #2, 3 and 4). Blackhill reported that soil readings in the channel were now field measured below 1.0mS/cm. Excavation points on both sides of the access road culvert are now acting as sumps for the collection of residual fluids. A water truck was stationed at these points today, recovering any collected fluids. The pad surface area that was determined to be impacted by the release has been excavated as much as possible (photos #6 and 7). Blackhill explained that collected fluids shown in photo #7 are also being recovered. Fluid in this area, which is located right next to the initial release point, was field measured at ~17.8mS/cm today. Blackhill reported that equipment will be brought in on either 4/11/2023 or 4/12/2023 to move the produced water tanks and associated secondary containment structure in order to excavate beneath them. The impacted stormwater basin has been emptied to where just a few puddles remain (photo #1). All water collected from the basin was stored in tanks shown in photo #9 and continues to be trucked offsite for disposal or reuse. I field measured a small puddle near the stormwater channel entry point of the basin which returned a reading of ~1.75mS/cm. All impacted materials that have been recovered are stored in lined and covered waste containers which are held on secondary containment (photo #8). All violations associated with the releases from 1/2/2023 and from 4/6/2023 remain outstanding at this time against API #015-23733. I departed the site at 1620 hours.As a follow-up to the violations cited on 4/6/2023, the DEP requests a summary of the quantity of fluids collected in regards to the produced water release, including the stormwater basin, and where the water was transported after collection. This information can be provided in the NOV response.

Comments: On 2/14/20 an incident inspection of the Beacon well pad was conducted in response to a spill (CTS ID: 347983) reported on 2/10/20. The following was observed: >>On 2/11/20 WQSS John Carson spoke with Greylock Representative Keith Eighmey who reported that while drilling using a filming agent foam from an open topped tank blew to the well pad and via a failed seam in the pad containment traveled to the pad's drainage ditches and then to the primary sediment basin and into the Waters of the Commonwealth (WOC; unnamed tributary to Frosty Run). The amount of material lost was reported as unknown but minimal. Operator sampling and MSDS were requested. >>At the time of inspection the sediment basin was found to be overflowing via the stand pipe resulting in substantial flow of sediment laden waters bypassing and flowing through site perimeter controls causing accelerated erosion and impact to the WOC. Additionally, the runoff stream and channel off site notably still bore multiple large piles of foam strongly indicating ongoing impact related to the reported spill. At the time of inspection dewatering/pumping out the impacted water from the sediment basin and appropriate disposal of the effluent as site waste was encouraged. Obstruction of the waterway was not approved. This spill and its impact constitutes a violation of 35 P.S. § 6018.301, 35 P.S. § 691.307(a), * 25 Pa. Code § 78a.54, 25 Pa. Code § 91.34(a), 25 Pa. Code § 102.5(m)4, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e), 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1, 25 Pa. Code § 102.11(a)1, 25 Pa. Code § 78a.53 in that the operator failed to control regulated materials in a manner that prevents pollution to the ground and Waters of the Commonwealth. Violations of 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(e) and 25 Pa. Code § 78a.64A(b)1 were related to the failure of site secondary containment and were shown to have been corrected by the operator prior to the time of inspection. >>A concurrent general surface inspection related to the site ESCGP (ESX16-059-0038) was conducted in response to observed site conditions, particularly multiple slope failures.

Comments: On March 25, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection was conducted to follow up to IR 3484420, where violations were left outstanding due to no Act 9 sign and Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (see photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack secondary containment, as is required at unconventional well sites (see photos 2, 4, and 5). The top hatch of the production tank closest to the well head closest to the well head was observed on the ground. The Department recommends that this top hatch is replaced onto the production tank to prevent possible overflowing with rainwater (see photo 6).The well postings on-site include contact information for Murphy Production, Inc. The well tag is affixed to the well head with Murphy Production Inc listed on the tag along with the permit number and well name (see photo 8, 11, and 13).No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the well head (see photo 10). The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (see photo 9). The Department recommends that equipment onsite that is not in use for production is removed from site.The access road is stabilized with gravel. The well is exhibiting greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion or sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (see photos 3 and 12).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued under IR 3484420 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

The well inactive status expired over four years ago on 04/26/2021. No production has ever been reported for this well. This is not an active, producing well. The well is abandoned. The well is required to be plugged. Continued Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Plugging Requirement OGA3220(A). At the time of inspection, 5 wells installed, but only 4 wells in production on well pad. Cleared Notice of violation (NOV) issued for Well posting OGA3211(G). This is a nonactive status, non-producing, abandoned oil and gas well that requires plugging. The Operator has stated in response correspondence to the Department, as mentioned above that 'To bring Whiting 1 into compliance with OGA 3220(A), Hilcorp is proposing to plug and abandon the well in accordance with PADEP regulations by June 30, 2026'. The Department concurs with the Operator response statements.

Comments: On October 13, 2022, the Department conducted a Routine inspection at the Sinay well pad in Sewickley Township, Westmoreland County. Present were myself, ET Marcella Dantzler, those listed from the SWDO OG Team, and EQT representatives Joe Eversman and Logan Dominick.The following was observed:The Act 9 sign was at the entrance of the access road, and was not obstructed by vegetation (see photo 2). A PPC plan was also in the office, but missing required components. Neither the secondary containment inspection records nor the well permit were available onsite when requested. A sediment basin was observed along the left side of the access road, looking towards the pad. A forebay cleanout was observed on the opposite side, with a culvert connecting them under the access road (see photo 5). Cattails were observed in the sediment basin. A further review will be conducted to ensure that they are part of the PCSM plan. A soil stockpile was observed along the left side of the access road, immediately before entering the pad (see photo 6). The operator was actively drilling onsite. This is the first well being drilled. The operator intends to drill 4 wells total. A destabilized area of soil was discovered behind the sound wall on the eastern side of the well pad (see photo 15). Preexisting metal and brick was observed outside of the LOD at this location, as was noted in the site E and S plans (see photo 16). A tear in the rig site containment was observed at the southern side of the pad. This was brought to Mr. Eversman's attention, who immediately called in a crew to repair it (see photo 12). Tanks and containers onsite that contained regulated substances were labelled, showed no evidence of leaks/discharges (see photos 13 and 14). The production tanks were within secondary containment (see photo 17). A puddle was observed at the northeastern corner of the containment. A soil conductivity reading was taken in this puddle, which read 200 Micro Siemens. The rig site containment appeared to be nearly full at its northeastern corner. A soil conductivity reading was taken at this corner, which read 390 Micro Siemens. The Department inquired with Mr. Eversman about whether the containment is pumped regularly. Mr. Eversman stated that the site containment gets pumped multiple times daily as needed. A pump truck later came to pump the containment during this inspection. A sediment-laden discharge to WOTC was discovered upon returning to the access road entrance (see photo 23). This discharge was flowing into a sewer drain that emptied into a field across the road from the well pad, through a culvert (see photo 21). This culvert was found to be approximately 80% full with sediment (see photo 22). Near the end of the inspection, EQT representative Logan Dominick arrived to the site, who was informed of the Department's findings. Mr. Dominick was able to provide an electronic copy of the PPC plan onsite, this was requested to be emailed to the Department for further review. He also stated to the Department that CFS and a silt pad will be installed around and over the sewer grate to prevent further discharge to the WOTC. Violations are being issued for discharging to the waters of the commonwealth, failing to have an adequate ER AND PPC plan onsite, failing to have the drill permit onsite, and failing to have secondary containment inspection records onsite.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 9/28/2021
Comments: On September 28, 2021, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a follow inspection to a reported spill at the Inflection Energy TLC Well Pad. The spill notification was received on September 26, 2021. The DEP met with Inflection Energy Zac Subra found an area of about 50 ft x 80 ft with variable conductivity levels from 1,200 uS/cm to 10,000 u/S/cm. The location of the spill was N 41.3335434, W -76.9287938. Inflection began excavation immediately. Upon arrival, the area of impact had been excavated and backfilled. The spill did not appear to leave the pad surface. The spill was caused by a hole in the containment and a leak in a flushing line used during the well stimulation process. An estimated volume of the leak will be determined when the remainder of the rig mats are removed and the area under the mats can be evaluated. Penn E&R collected confirmatory samples on September 27, 2021. Inflection Energy is in the process of setting up for flow back on the recently stimulated wells. The MASS and freshwater AST still remain on site. This spill causes violations of the Clean Streams Law Section 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301. The DEP recommends beginning the Act 2 process when the rig mats are completely removed due to the unknown volume of the spill.

Comments: Please note, violations were cited on May 9, 2024 for a brine release. A copy of that inspection report and NOV was emailed and mailed to the operator. The mailed letter was returned to the Department with the envelope stating "return to sender" from the USPS. Please note, that the Department never received a NOV response letter either.I conducted a follow-up site inspection on July 17, 2024. Flakey paint and corrosion was observed on the production equipment and axillary pipes. The Department recommends monitoring the equipment and repainting or replacing the equipment if needed. A 5x Altair gas meter was used to screen around the production equipment. A gas leak was detected on the well head, see photo #5 and 6. Combustible gas exceeded the meters range, methane reading was 2% LEL and CO was 31 ppm. The Department recommends addressing the gas leak and notifying me once this is completed. The case will be referred to a Departments OGI for follow-up.Please note, the chart recorder has not been changed in months. The well tag has the previous operators name and contact information listed on. The Department recommends updating the contact information.The brine tank continues to drip brine fluids onto the ground. The leak is coming from the valve set area on the brine tank. A screw has been inserted into the brine tank to help stop the leak. Drips were observed coming out of the leak area. During the inspection I observed a dead spot of vegetation extending approximately 55' long and approximately 16' in the widest spot. The soil was inundated with deer tracks. I used a soil Hanna Groline soil probe to screen for conductivity. All readings exceeded the meters range of 4.00 mS/cm. Fluids still remain within the poly brine tank and the well is active. The Department recommends addressing the brine release. Violations remain outstanding.

Violation ID: 8226586
Permit API: 129-28077
Unconventional: No

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/24/2025
Comments: On March 24, 2025, the Department conducted a follow up Inspection of the RWS Development 001 Well in response to an incident which is documented in IR 3941481 and 3941519 where violations were issued for a brine release. Present during today's inspection was operator representative Ronald Seich.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed charred vegetation on a slope adjacent to the well site, no erosion or sedimentation issues were observed. A wellhead was observed with a well tag fixed to it with all required information posted on it, and no active fluid leaks or fluid discharges were observed coming from or near this wellhead. All other production equipment was observed removed and loaded/being loaded onto a trailer for disposal.It appeared excavation had been started in the area where the production equipment was removed. Excavated material/soil was observed loaded onto tarps. No excavation appeared to have been started on the ditch. Mr. Seich stated that they planned on having all excavation completed, including the ditch, by the end of the day. He also stated that Moody would be onsite tomorrow (3/25/2022) to perform a site assessment and collect samples to evaluate their remediation.A soil conductivity reading was taken in the area where the production tank was previously located with a reading of 0.34mS. The Department observed standing fluid in the ditch/channel in several locations. Conductivity readings were taken of the fluid in the ditch in several locations with readings of 16.00mS, 9.16mS, 2.30mS, 0.87mS, 0.83mS, and 0.80mS. The conductivity readings appeared to decrease with distance from the well/production tank. No standing fluid was observed in the ditch in approximately the last 45 feet prior to terminating near the stream. There did not appear to be a recent flow path of fluid in the section of ditch from the last location of standing water to the remainder of ditch before the stream. A conductivity reading was taken in this area of the ditch with a reading of 0.34mSA conductivity reading was then taken in the stream in the area where the ditch appears to terminate prior to the stream with a reading of 0.73mS. No sheen, discoloration, or foaming was observed in the stream.Based on the Department's observations and conductivity readings obtained, it appears that the conductivity readings are comparable to the previous inspections in regards to distance and levels of elevated readings in the ditch. It appears that released fluids may have been contained to the portions of the ditch where standing fluid was observed, and it did not appear from the observations and readings that there was a release into Waters of the Commonwealth.Bases on today's inspection, violations remain outstanding.

Comments: On 07/07/2025 a representative from the Pennsylvania Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted a routine inspection of Greylock Production LLCs Ron multi-well pad located in Hector Township, Potter County. Upon arrival to the site at 1030 hours, weather was 83F and partly cloudy. An Act 9 sign and well permits are posted at the site entrance (photo #1).No standing water was observed on the pad surface.The Patterson 582 drilling rig is noted onsite; the Ron 3UH well has been drilled and the rig is currently drilling the Ron 4UH well, the Ron 5UH has yet to be drilled (photo #2). The backyard drill cuttings processing area remains tidy and there is no evidence of spills or releases (photo #3). The cement mixing area is stationed on rig matting and upright water storage tanks as well as oil tanks are noted for cement mixing and production of oil-based mud (photo #4). The chemical storage area is also held in a secondary containment structure and is separate from the rig matting (photo #5).1 gas processing units (GPUs) are also located onsite (photo #6). The GPUs are stationed in a secondary containment structure which held less than 10% standing water. There are 4 produced fluid tanks located onsite and stationed in secondary containment (photo #7); the containment structure contained less than 10% standing water. A dehydration unit is also noted onsite and stationed in a secondary containment structure (photo #8).Numerous temporary storage tanks are located onsite for flow back activities for the Ron 1UH and Ron 2UH; these tanks are held in a secondary containment structure (photo #9).A weekly E and S inspection log is available for review and was last updated on 06/23/2025 (photo #10). Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/01/2023
Comments: This follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions after multiple releases on Pad B for which violations remain outstanding. Both pads and the access road were snow-covered during this inspection. The completions operations have ceased on Pad B and the snubbing rigs and their associated equipment have been removed from the pad. I met with EQT representative Zac Subra upon arriving on Pad B. A representative from Creston Environmental was present on location as well. A crew was working on installing the GPUs on the pad. Trenches were being dug for the flow lines which will run from the well heads to the GPUs on the west side of the pad. A large trench was present at the well heads. Some fluid was seeping into this trench from the fill material surrounding the well cellar for well B-11H. The electrical conductivity (EC) of this fluid was 2.45 mS/cm. A vacuum truck was sucking up this fluid during this inspection. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up any elevated EC fluid found on the pad surface or during excavation on the pad. The modular aboveground storage structure (MASS) was empty during this inspection. A work crew was beginning to disassemble the MASS during this inspection. The north central area of the well pad has been excavated. One area is a long horizontal area approximately two feet of the north stormwater channel. The EC of the fluid here was 3.35 to 5.41 mS/cm. Another excavated area is to the southwest. According to Mr. Subra, EQT believes that the produced fluid that had been released to this area flowed along an area that had previously been excavated in association with a release that occurred during drilling operations on the well pad. Mr. Subra also said that the northwest area of the well pad where clamshell boxes had led to a release in the dancefloor area has been fully excavated. Additional excavation would still need to occur in the north central area of the well pad as well as in the northeast corner of the pad where the MASS still is present, he also stated. The lined sump remains at the east outlet of the north stormwater channel.Violations remain outstanding for the reported release of produced fluid to the surface of Pad B.

Comments: On July 10, 2025, the Department conducted a Routine Complete Inspection of Burnett Oil Co Inc's Stickle Ross Mountain Unit 1H located in Fairfield Township, Westmoreland County following an Oil and Gas Inspector referral during IR 4010435 where the Department observed the following:"There are two areas that appear to have oil staining. The area Southeast of the well is where the pump was during plugging and is approximately 25feet long and extends under the frac tank. The area North of the plugged well has several smaller spots 1-3 feet in diameter, and is where the rig was placed during plugging."Accompanying during today's inspection is Tyler Metzger (WQS DEP).At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an Act 9 sign at the access road entrance to not be in compliance and inside the on-site mailbox was an outdated Emergency Response Plan (ERP). Violations for the Act 9 Sign and the ERP are being issued under 129-28411.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the Stickle well site to have 2 wells on it. The 1H: 129- 28411 well appears to be in production, while the 1H: 129-28648 appeared to be plugged with a vented monument. A well marker was observed to be leaning up against the wellhead with the well's permit number and a plug date of 7/17/2018, however, according to Department inspection records, this well was reportedly re-plugged on 7/1/2025. The Department is requesting Oil and Gas Inspector follow-up for evaluation of compliance for the well marker. The Department did not observe any active fluid leaks or fluid discharges coming from or near this reportedly re-plugged well. At the time of this inspection, the Department observed the two frac tanks, the half round flow back tank and the trailer that were observed during IR 4010435 to be removed from the well site. The 25' long oil stain where the frac tanks were, along with multiple oil stained spots where the rig was sitting were observed on the graveled well pad. The oily substance did not have a sheen but had an unrecognizable odor. The Department screened the oil stained areas with a conductivity meter and collected readings of 0.1422 mS, 0.215 mS, and 0.0019 mS. The Department also observed darker soil around the plugged well, therefore this area was screened as well and a reading of 0.0343 mS was collected. The Department also observed a metallic gold thick substance on the gravel in one of the oil stains, this substance appears to be pipe sealant. The Department recommends the Operator remediate these release(s) in accordance with 78a66(c)(1).The Operator is requested to submit a written response within seven (7) days of the receipt of this report. This written response should include an incident report, a timeline of remedial measures, and a plan for remediation of the spill or release.The Department is also requesting the Operator clarify what the oily substance(s) is, how the release was quantified and submit the waste manifest from the site remediation upon receipt.Based on today's inspection, violations shall be issued for the oily substance(s) on the graveled well pad.

Comments: On May 17, 2022, I conducted an inspection of the Ziolkowski 11771 Well Site in Findlay Township, Allegheny County. The inspection was conducted in response to a release reported to the Department on 5/17/2022 at 12:23am. According to the report at 11:15pm, a water hauler released approximately 40 barrels of brine water to the well pad and access road. During the inspection, I observed staining along the east side of Potato Garden Road leading from the well site access road heading north toward State Route 30. I was accompanied by RRC representative Nate Smiell. The Act 9 sign was installed. The PPC plan and ER plan were on site I observed staining on the north side of the access road from the wells site entrance up to the well pad. The staining appeared to be approximately 4’ to 6’ in width, the impacted depth was estimated to be between 2" and 6" deep depending on the specific location. The Operator was in the process of scraping the stained material from the access road with a small bulldozer and loading roll off boxes with a skid steer. The Operator had progressed from the well site entrance up the access road approximately 400’. The Operator excavated the impacted material from the well pad and placed the material in roll off disposal boxes. The impacted area appeared to be approximately 480’ in length, 35’ wide with a depth of 4" to 6". The total length of the impacted area at the location (well and access road) is approximately 1,700’, with varying widths and depths. The release did not appear to reach waters of the commonwealth from the well site or access road and did not appear to impact the PCSM basins on site. The release appeared to be contained to the well pad, access road and sections the channel adjacent to the access road. Violation are being issued for the release of a regulated fluid. I recommend that the Operator continue to follow the Departments most recent spill policy for remediation of spills greater than 42 gallons.

Comments: On July 8 2025, the Department conducted an inspection of the McMichael Well Pad in regards to a spill that was reported to the Department on July 8 2025 at 9:12am . Present during the inspection was Brandon Carson.The findings are as follows:At the time of the inspection, the Act 9 sign was posted at the access road entrance in accordance with 78a55. The Emergency Response Plan (ERP), and the Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency Plan (PPC), both of which contained all required components, were located within the on-site mailbox. The access road appeared to be stabilized with gravel.Upon arrival at the well site remediation efforts appeared to be nearing completion as the remaining excavated material was being placed into the roll off dumpster. Mr. Carson identified the location of the spill. According to Mr. Carson, ,the spill (which occurred on 7/8/2025 at 7:15am) was reportedly caused by a 2" hydraulic line failing on the snubbing unit during work on the 14H well. This resulted in a release of hydraulic fluid to secondary containment as well as the graveled well pad. Comments: During a routine complete inspection on 5/16/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3788146), I noted API 065-26269 did not have a well tag, equipment not necessary for production was being stored on site, and there was evidence of a production fluid release greater than 42 gallons.During a follow up inspection (FUI) on 6/26/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3790440), I noted the well had a new well tag, the pipe was moved across the access road, and the spill area was seeded and mulched. The Department did not receive a response from the Notice of Violation with the operators intentions to use either the Act 2 or the Alternative Remediation Process. The Department did not receive tipping receipts or waste manifests associated with removal and disposal of contaminated soil from the spill. The tag violation was closed. The other violations remained open.On a FUI on 8/19/2024 (Inspection Record No. 3816085), I noted the Department still hasn't received tipping receipts or waste manifests regarding the clean up of this site. I emailed Ray Hepler information about Act 2 remediation. On 8/28/2024, Jack Crow, Henry Kramer, Brian Shank and myself met with Ray Hepler at the PA DEP Meadville Regional Office to discuss the outstanding violations at the Wheeler property. Ray Hepler stated he had the contaminated soil from the brine releases on a roll off and would send us the manifests soon. The Department received a manifest for waste on 9/9/2024. However, the manifest stated the soil was "Beaver-PA 100%". The manifest also stated the soil was hauled in a "white pick up truck", but during the 8/28/2024 meeting Ray Hepler stated the soil was in a roll off container. This manifest does not show the proper disposal of the soil from the Wheeler W12 well site located in Jefferson County. Today (9/12/2024), Brian Shank and I conducted a FUI. The pipe not necessary for production was still being stored near the access road. The spill area appeared to have new top soil and grass seed. We collected soil conductivity readings throughout the spill area. A background soil conductivity reading was collected. The soil conductivity reading was 154.5 pS/cm. Near the production tank, the soil conductivity reading was 3.28 mS/cm. Approximately 4 feet from the production tank, the soil conductivity reading 1416 pS/cm. These readings indicate that the prior spill has not been remediated yet. We collected grab soil samples to send to the Department's accredited laboratory. The samples will be analyzed for SAC 960 and UVIR.The outstanding violations for the Wheeler W12 well site will remain open at this time.

Permit API: 125-23051
Unconventional: No

Municipality: West Pike Run Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/03/2024
Comments: On 06/03/2024, an incident inspection was conducted at the Zemba 1 well site following receipt of a spill report submitted by the operator on 05/31/2024 (CTS 381125). Penneco representatives on site. I called the operator on 06/03/2024 and they said that approximately 5 to 6 barrels were spilled on site and that the tank was cracked. The incident was discovered 05/31/2024 at 11:30 am and was reported to the Department on 05/31/2024 at 3:00 pm.Conductivity probe calibrated on 06/03/2024.The following was observed:The operator and well's information were posted on site, however the first three digits of the API were reading 126 instead of 125. I recommend that this is addressed. The tag on the well was displaying the last six digits of the API and not 125 (Photos 1, 2).Conductivity readings were taken at the site in the area that appeared to be impacted. A section of grass was dead and discolored near the tank (Photos 3-5). Readings were taken before and after calibration of the conductivity probe.Readings before calibration ranged from 25.4-852 uS/cm (Photos 6-9).Readings after calibration ranged from 227-1142 uS/cm (Photos 10-16).The tank was removed and additional readings were taken within the area with focus on the wet spots (Photos 17, 18). Readings were 20.5 uS/cm and 205 uS/cm (Photos 19, 20).The wellhead was in generally good condition with some corrosion (Photo 21).The Department requests the type of material released (brine or oil). The Department recommends that the Spill Policy is utilized due to a spill larger than 42 gallons. The Department also requests information on why the remediation was not started and/or the spill immediately addressed. Due to the observation of dead grass which is indicative of a fluid impact from the well site, violations of 78.54, SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78.66(b), and 78.66(e) are being issued.

Comments: On 10/11/2024, I conducted an inspection at the Blacksville I BIP32 Well in Wayne Township, Greene County in response to a Notice of Intent (NOI) to plug a well The NOI was received by The Department on 9/9/2024 and 10/1/2024 due to plugging schedule changes.On site at the time of inspection were contractors associated with well plugging. The contractors indicated that the plugging rig was set up on 10/8/2024, and they expected the plugging operation to take 3 days to complete.While on site I observed the following:-The access road appeared to be in generally good condition. I recommend that the Rock Construction Entrance (RCE) installed along the access road receive additional aggregate if contractors expect to be on site for additional time (Photos 1-6).-I observed a silt fence filled with sediment at STA 14+00. I observed sediment that bypassed the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entered a stream identified by E and S plans as UNT to Dunkard Creek. Scouring left of the culvert outlet was evident where sediment bypassed the silt fence. Sediment accumulation was evident throughout the streambed and significant sediment buildup was present within the culvert outlet. I followed sediment within the streambed for approximately 50 feet below the culvert outlet (Photos 7-15).-I observed no sediment accumulation above the timber matting crossing at the culvert inlet, indicating that sediment entered the stream where it bypassed the perimeter silt fence (Photo 16).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 15+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 17).-A material stockpile staged along the access road at STA 18+00 was bordered by reinforced silt fence and was temporarily stabilized with straw (Photo 18).-The plugging rig was installed at the time of inspection. All equipment was staged on the plugging pad. I was unable to see if secondary containment was installed at the plugging rig due to equipment being staged close to the rig (Photos 21-22).-The plugging pad perimeter was lined with reinforced silt fence, which appeared to be functioning properly. I observed no signs of accelerated erosion around the plugging pad (Photos 23-24).Due to sediment bypassing the silt fence at STA 14+00 and entering UNT to Dunkard Creek, violations of 102.4(b)1, 102.11(a)1, 78.53, CSL 301, and CSL 307(a) are being issued.

Violation ID: 908264

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 2/17/2021
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protetion (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM - Headwaters 145 Well Pad located in Ulysses Twp, Potter Co. on 2/18/21 @ 1130 hours. The weather was 16 degree and sunny. Snow with a coating of ice has accumulated on the site. Joe Harrick and Ron Burdick of JKLM and Terra Tokarz, Whipper Hill Consulting were present onsite for the inspections. On 2/13/21, Mr. Harrick called to report a release of 80-120 gallons of production fluid on the Headwaters 145 Well Pad. JKLM was in the process of transferring fluid from the production tanks to the Headwaters Tank Farm, when a hose connected to the pump let loose releasing the fluid to the containment and the pad surface. A nearby vac truck was able to remove the standing liquid from the contaiment and the well pad, estimated to be approximately 1 barrel. At the time of this inspection, JKLM has removed the majority of the impacted pad material. An excavated area approximately 15' x 20' was observed on the Northeast side of the well pad located between the permanent tan-colored production tanks and the green-colored extra storage tanks. The excavation is between 6" and 24" deep. The excavation was impeded by frozen ground conditions and the location of buried dump lines. Some "hand work" was done to remove material around the above ground port for the waterline use to transfer the production fluid to the tank farm. At the time of the spill the E&S discharge points at the corners of the well pad were shut-in. JKLM stated no production fluid entered the E&S controls or left the site. A total of 8 rolloff containers of impacted snow, ice and pad material have been removed from the site. JKLM believes the majority of impacted material has been excavated. JKLM stated they plan to replace all existing hoses onsite to discourage a similar event. Penn E&R will be onsite to conduct confirmatory samples when weather allows. Due to the volume of the release, JKLM confirmed they plan to demonstrate attainment of Act 2 standards. This release is referred to the DEP Cleanups and Brownfields Program. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time: CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 25 Pa Code 78a57 I departed the site at 1315 hours.

Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/12/2022
Comments: Site inspection conducted as a follow up to Notice of Violations (NOV) associated inspection report #3373528 dated 6/6/2022 and administrative inspection report #3386649 dated 7/5/2022. There are no Blackhill Energy personnel on site at time of inspection. Weather conditions are overcast and 31 degrees F. During this inspection, completions equipment is still attached to the wells drilled and stimulated during 2021. Two sand separators and a 500 barrel gas buster tank appear to be connected to gas wells (photo 2). Puddled fluid on site was screened using an Oakton PCTS 50 water conductivity meter and a Hanna Groline soil conductivity meter. While screening puddles around the well heads and 500 barrel gas buster frac tank, the Department observed fluid draining from the tank and releasing onto secondary containment (photo 3). The containment is open along the north end discharge port and puddled fluid on containment appears to be flowing off containment into the pad surface (photo 4). Water within containment is observed with conductivity reading 'Over Range' (>19.99 mS/cm). Puddles screened outside of containment are observed to range between 9.8 mS/cm near the north well head to 'Over Range' in a puddle next to the tank secondary containment. Sample 4406-018 collected at 11:45 from fluid puddled on pad rock surface between tank secondary containment and north-most gas well (photo 7). Sample will be analyzed using SAC 942. The Department notified Regina Logue, Blackhill Energy Environmental Manager, that the tank was leaking at 12:15. Ms. Logue indicated that Blackhill personnel were en route to the site and that Moody's Environmental was contracted to conduct site characterization. Violation noted for potential pollution. Additional violations may be issued pending results of water sample analysis. Previous NOV's associated with inspection report #3373528 dated 6/6/2022 and administrative inspection report #3386649 dated 7/5/2022 remain outstanding.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72-hr (Stepped) pressure build-up tests, (SPBUT) being performed on all (6) wells on the Aukema pad. The Aukema 3H, 4H, 7H, 1HC, 2HC and the 101HC wells. These tests are being performed to assess the results of the initial remedial deployment of Renegades localized casing expansion tool in the production casing of the Aukema 1HC and 101HC wells on 5/17/21 and 5/18/21 and the 3H and 2HC between 1/24 - 27/21. This is the second round of testing since initial remedial work was performed. SPBUTs were initiated on 12/6/21 @ ~ 08:45 and progressed by shutting in the outer most annuli of each well for first 24-hrs, then in 24-hr progressions, sequentially shutting in the next inner annuli, resulting in a total 72-hr SPBUT. - All (6) wells annuli are shut in. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Reps. Trey Sites amd Dalton Johnson and Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andrew Pfisterer. Starting at approx. 09:00, ending annuli pressures were checked using a Digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. Creston Consultants collected gas samples off annuli, where present, and will send out for isotopic analysis.
